questions.q: Name the mountain range that acts as a boundary for the Western Coastal Plain.
questions.a: The Western Ghats. A wrong answer suggests the student is confusing the mountain ranges, likely forgetting that the Western Ghats run parallel to the western coastline.

questions.q: Why is the Western Coastal Plain considered "narrower" than the Eastern Coastal Plain?
questions.a: It is narrower because the Western Ghats mountains are situated very close to the Arabian Sea, leaving little space for a plain. A wrong answer indicates the student has not visualized the physical barrier of the mountains.

questions.q: If you were a farmer living on the Malabar coast, which crop would you likely grow, and why is the climate suitable?
questions.a: You would grow coconuts and spices. The climate is suitable because this region receives heavy monsoon rainfall, which these crops require to thrive. A wrong answer shows a lack of connection between climate (rainfall) and agricultural output.

questions.q: Compare the location of the Konkan coast and the Coromandel coast.
questions.a: The Konkan coast is on the Western side (Maharashtra/Goa), while the Coromandel coast is on the Eastern side (Tamil Nadu/Andhra Pradesh). A wrong answer indicates a failure to orient "West" vs "East" on the Indian map.

questions.q: Is it accurate to say the Western Coastal Plain is dry compared to the East? Explain your judgment.
questions.a: No, this is incorrect; the Western coast is actually quite wet as it receives heavy monsoon rainfall. This shows the student misunderstands the climate patterns of the Indian subcontinent.

questions.q: Design a simple travel brochure comparing a trip to the Konkan coast versus the Coromandel coast. What would be the main difference you mention?
questions.a: The answer should highlight the narrow, mountain-backed scenery of the Konkan coast versus the broader, river-delta plains of the Coromandel. A poor answer fails to differentiate the physical geography of the two regions.
